faq.a: Salih is associated with the Arabic form صَالِح, whose core sense is salih; righteous; a prophet.

faq.q: What is the origin of Salih?
faq.a: Salih is associated with Arabic. Salih is Arabic صَالِح (Ṣāliḥ), meaning 'righteous'; it is the name of a prophet in the Quran.
Yes — the underlying form صَالِح is Arabic.
Salih can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Salih should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Ṣāliḥ occurs in the Quran as the name of a prophet.

faq.q: What does Salih mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Salih is rendered صالح and carries the sense صالح، نیک؛ نبی.

faq.q: What does Salih mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Salih is rendered صالح and carries the sense صالح، صالح؛ پیامبر.
A romanized syllable approximation is sa-lih. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Salih?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Salih, salih. Script forms are صالح, صَالِح, सालिह.

faq.q: Is Salih a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
